stop_reassessed.verdict: THE STOP WAS A FALSE POSITIVE OF THIS RUN'S OWN DETECTOR, NOT AN OFF-LIST ADMIT.
stop_reassessed.what_the_run_stopped_on: off_list_admits on GET /api/scoped/amgt/watchlist for cottonwood and inflection
stop_reassessed.the_measurement: all THREE arms returned HTTP 200 with body length 2 and the IDENTICAL fingerprint 4f53cda18c2baa0c (an empty JSON container). No off-list data was served: the route does not read selected_tenant and answered the same empty list for every firm.
stop_reassessed.the_defect: the ALL detector required own_len > 80 before classifying an identical-fingerprint 2xx as selector_ignored. That floor existed to stop SHORT SHARED REFUSAL ENVELOPES reading as selector-ignored, but it also sent a SHORT IDENTICAL 200 into the admit bucket. The discriminator should be the fingerprint alone. Fixed in sa_r1b_run.py after this run: length now annotates and never classifies.
stop_reassessed.consequence: the hops did not run. NOTE SEPARATELY that hop (e) would have failed anyway -- it polls GET /api/scoped/investor-reporting/analysis/requests/{requestId}, one of the 7 irpt-status routes measured 500 in this same run (see irpt_status_regression). The defect cost the attempt, not the outcome.

NO_FIRM_expected.reading: census verdict NO_FIRM. The pair's own blast radius v2 already states the 51 NO_FIRM routes stay reachable as for any opal-capital user, so an ignored selector here is the KNOWN class and not a new finding. GET /api/scoped/amgt/watchlist belongs here too: empty for every firm.

no_selected_tenant_carrier.reading: census verdict MORE_THAN_ONE, but these two take NO selected_tenant: the ticket plane is clamped by _in_profile_scope on the TICKET's requester.firm, not by the selector. Identical bytes across arms is therefore expected and proves nothing either way about the clamp. The clamp's positive evidence is the LIST: 8 tickets returned, distinct requester firms ['49financial'] only. Applying a selector test to a route with no selector was a category error in this run's instrument.
